question.problem:
For the universal set $U,$ given by

$$
U=\{2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9\},
$$

find the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x)$ for the following predicates: 

- $P(x):$ $x$ is prime.

- $Q(x):$ $3\,|\,x.$
question.worked_solution:
Since we have that

$$
P(x)⇔Q(x)≡(P(x)∧Q(x))∨(¬P(x)∧¬Q(x)),
$$

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇔Q}=({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q})\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that:

- The truth set of $P(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{P}=\{2,3,5,7\}
$$

and its complement is

$$
{\overset{―}{T}}_{P}=\{4,6,8,9\}.
$$

- The truth set of $Q(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{Q}=\{3,6,9\}
$$

 
and its complement is

$$
{\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}=\{2,4,5,7,8\}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q} & =\{2,3,5,7\}\cap \{3,6,9\} \\  & =\{3\} \\ {\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q} & =\{4,6,8,9\}\cap \{2,4,5,7,8\} \\  & =\{4,8\} \\ {T}_{P⇔Q} & =({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}) \\  & =\{3\}\cup \{4,8\} \\  & =\{3,4,8\}.\end{aligned}
$$
